facts.statement: Agujaceratops was originally classified under the genus Chasmosaurus before being moved to its own genus.
The genus Agujaceratops was named by Lucas, Sullivan, and Hunt in 2006.
facts.quote: Agujaceratops was named by Spencer G. Lucas, Robert M. Sullivan and Adrian Hunt in 2006

facts.statement: Agujaceratops lived in western Texas during the Late Cretaceous period, specifically the Campanian age.
facts.quote: Agujaceratops (meaning "horned face from Aguja") is a genus of chasmosaurine ceratopsid dinosaur from the Late Cretaceous (Campanian) of western Texas

facts.statement: Agujaceratops was a large dinosaur measuring about 4.3 meters in length and weighing 1.5 metric tons.
facts.quote: Agujaceratops was a relatively large horned dinosaur, reaching 4.3 m in length and 1.5 MT in body mass

facts.statement: The back of the Agujaceratops frill has a strong notch creating a heart shape, accompanied by three or four pairs of spike-like hornlets.
facts.quote: The back of the frill has a strong notch, as in Pentaceratops and Chasmosaurus, giving it a heart shape, with three or four pairs of spike-like hornlets

facts.statement: The edges of the Agujaceratops frill have numerous low, blunt hornlets that create a strongly scalloped appearance.
facts.quote: The edges of the frill bear numerous low, blunt hornlets, giving it a strongly scalloped appearance

facts.statement: The brow horns of Agujaceratops are oriented upward and outward, curving backward when viewed from the side.
facts.quote: The brow horns are oriented up and out, and curve backwards in side view

facts.statement: Agujaceratops was a quadrupedal herbivore, like other ceratopsids.
facts.quote: Like other ceratopsids, Agujaceratops was a four-legged plant eater

facts.statement: The elaborate frill and horns of Agujaceratops suggest a complex social life involving displays and fights over territory or mating.
facts.quote: The elaborate frill and horns suggest a complex social life, perhaps involving displays towards and fights with other members of the species over territory or mating

facts.statement: During the time Agujaceratops lived, the Aguja Formation was located along the western margin of the Western Interior Seaway.
facts.quote: At the time, the Aguja Formation lay along the western margin of the Western Interior Seaway

facts.statement: The habitat where Agujaceratops fossils were found may have been a swamp, based on the nature of the sediments.
facts.quote: The habitat Agujaceratops lived in (at least where the fossil material was found) may have been a swamp, due to the nature of the sediments

facts.statement: Agujaceratops could reach nearly 5 meters in length, 3 meters in height, and weigh 2 tons.
facts.quote: Agujaceratops fue un dinosaurio con cuernos que llegó a medir cerca de 5 metros de largo y 3 de alto y a pesar 2 toneladas

facts.statement: Agujaceratops was found in the strata of the Aguja Formation in the state of Texas, USA.
facts.quote: Fue encontrado en los estratos de la Formación Aguja en el estado de Texas EE. UU.

facts.statement: Agujaceratops material was found in 1938 in Big Bend National Park by William Strain.
facts.quote: Encontrado en 1938, en el Parque nacional Big Bend por William Strain

facts.statement: Agujaceratops lived approximately between 75 and 70 million years ago during the Campanian in what is now North America.
facts.quote: hace aproximadamente entre 75 y 70 millones de años durante del Campaniense en lo que es hoy Norteamérica

facts.statement: The time range for Agujaceratops is estimated to be between 83.6 and 72.2 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Campanian to Campanian (83.6 to 72.2 million years ago)

rejected.statement: Agujaceratops featured a short nose horn, long brow horns, and a frill surrounded by small hornlets, similar to Pentaceratops.
rejected.quote: It was similar to other chasmosaurines such as Pentaceratops in having a short nose horn, long brow horns, and an elongate frill circled by small hornlets
